correctness.rationale: For equal cyclic shifts an unnormalized off-diagonal overlap is 1+omega or 1+omega^2, a negative cube root of unity; for distinct shifts the supports meet at one coordinate and the overlap is a negative cube root of unity directly. Normalization divides the overlap by 2. The charge-three addition kernel then yields constant off-diagonal -a_q/8, unit diagonal, and the two orthogonal eigenspaces as stated. Harmonic dimension follows by subtracting the lower-bidegree trace dimension. I independently checked every q=0..899 by exact evaluation of the Jacobi binomial sum, not the uploaded recurrence, with /workspace/branches/audit_exact.py. For the infinite tail, writing R(e^{it})=e^{it/2} times a square root of (1+2 cos t) gives the two boundary inequalities by orthogonality on the indicated arcs. The algebraic partners give products z and -3z so there are no interior zeros of the two factors; at z=0 they are 2. The minimum modulus principle gives the interior bounds. Separation of the two branch points and Cauchy's inequality give |p_q|<30 sqrt(q+1)<q+1 for q>=900. For q=1, a_q=-5/4, neither eigenvalue vanishes. At q=0,2 the pseudoinverse gives the stated norm on the actual phased mean-zero image; rephasing changes that hyperplane by diagonal unitaries. No dependence on an uploaded executable.
